Stones.notes: Closed source; read out of the compiled binary. Outputs 0 and 2 are written from the same register at 0xe6cc and 0xe6e0 and always carry the identical signal, so both are tagged to the same line. The sustain CV is added to a knob whose range is 0 to 1, so one volt covers the whole control and there is no clamp on the total: above 1V the envelope and the outputs go past 10V. Bound.notes: Closed source; read out of the compiled binary. Each channel's CV jack multiplies its level knob rather than adding to it, at a tenth per volt, so a cable resting at 0V silences that channel and the knob does nothing while it is in. One light is configured and follows the switch, but it has no position in the census and cannot be clicked.

Libra.notes: Closed source; read out of the compiled binary. The cutoff knob is configured 1.30103 to 4 and process() raises ten to that number, so the knob spans 20Hz to 10000Hz and the FREQ jack moves it by a decade per volt rather than an octave. Lyra.notes: Closed source; read out of the compiled binary. The gate opening is the strike envelope plus the level, clamped to 0 and 1; it sets both the amplifier gain and the corner of two cascaded one pole filters, whose angular frequency is 628.3185 at the bottom and 151424.77 at the top, which is 100Hz and 24100Hz. The LEVEL jack multiplies the knob rather than adding to it, at a tenth per volt, so a cable resting at 0V silences the module. The Decay knob is a rate, not a time: process() multiplies the envelope by the exponential of minus the knob times the sample period each sample, so a higher setting is a shorter decay. The two knobs have no lettering on the panel.
